name: FRED - 30-Year Fixed Rate Mortgage Average in the United States (MORTGAGE30US)
update_frequency: weekly (Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey, published Thursdays)
license: UNVERIFIED - do not build until confirmed. MORTGAGE30US is FRED's redistribution of Freddie Mac's Primary Mortgage Market Survey (PMMS), not a pure government series. Freddie Mac's general Content Use Policy prohibits selling, republishing, or retransmitting its site content without prior written consent, but carves out an exception letting sites publish 'automatically updated data' like PMMS without that consent, under a limited non-exclusive royalty-free license 'subject to... the terms and conditions for syndication' (not found in this search). It is unclear whether that exception covers ingesting the series into a commercial product's own data pipeline/database (as opposed to embedding a live widget), which is exactly what this project would do. Confirm Freddie Mac's syndication terms, or use FRED's own API terms (which are separately permissive) with clear PMMS attribution, before implementing.
cost: Free. Two access paths: (1) JSON/XML via api.stlouisfed.org/fred/series/observations with a free API key (instant self-serve registration at fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/api_key.html), rate-limited to 120 requests/60s per key; (2) a keyless CSV endpoint (fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=MORTGAGE30US) that needs no registration at all. Note: this session's network proxy blocked a live fetch of the CSV endpoint (CONNECT tunnel 403), so the exact current value below is from a cached search snapshot, not independently verified this run.
auth: none required for the CSV path; free instant API key for the JSON path (same pattern as CENSUS_API_KEY already used by app/sources/census_acs.py)
history: Weekly observations back to April 1971 - 50+ years, far more than enough for any backtest window this project uses.
integration_notes: app/scoring/investment.py sets `interest_rate: float = 0.065` as the default on the `Assumptions` dataclass (backend/app/scoring/investment.py:21) - a stale default a user can presumably override, not a hardcoded floor, but nothing currently refreshes it from reality. This series would feed that single default directly: a small adapter (kind not covered by existing kinds - closest is a new lightweight 'macro' kind, or simplest as an AppSetting written on refresh) would fetch the latest weekly value and use it as the suggested default interest_rate, instead of a constant that silently drifts (one cached search snapshot showed ~7.40% for the week of Oct 15, 2026 vs. the 6.5% default, a ~0.9pp gap - treat this specific figure as unverified pending a live fetch). Also note MORTGAGE30US covers conforming, prime-borrower 30-year fixed loans only and excludes jumbo/FHA/VA/ARM - many NYC condo purchases exceed the conforming loan limit, so this series is a reasonable default/benchmark but not a precise fit for every loan this product models. This is not a NeighborhoodMetric/pillar input - it's a single national macro input, so it sits outside the Growth Score pillars entirely and wouldn't need a new MetricDef.
recommendation: Conditional recommend. This is the cleanest gap of everything checked this run - investment.py has a stale, never-refreshed interest-rate default, and this is the standard series for exactly that number, with trivial no-key access and 50+ years of history. But two things hold it back from a flat recommend: (1) the redistribution/commercial-use terms for Freddie Mac's PMMS data are genuinely unclear from public documentation and need direct confirmation before shipping, and (2) the series excludes jumbo loans, which matters for a chunk of NYC condo purchases. Confirm the license question first; if it clears, this is still low-cost (one scalar, no geography join) and worth building ahead of any neighborhood-pillar candidate.
